messages:
anya: noticed a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate starting ~7:10 UTC, backend cpu+rx spikes. some requests fell through the cache and spiked redis RPS 
kevin: ouch. any correlate with deploys or kernel selection changes? 
mike: saw a rollout of runtime-2.3.1 ~7:05 that changed small-kernel heuristics and aggressive eviction thresholds. p50 ok but p95/p99 increased +120ms. 
anya: adding logs: 
```
[07:09:58] kv-cache miss prefix_key=chat_v2:prompt:0x7f4a:len=64
[07:09:58] fallback -> backend serve id=pool-13 req=0x9c3
[07:09:59] backend queue latency 320ms
[07:10:01] kv-cache eviction key=chat_v2:prompt:0x7f4a reason=memory_pressure
```
kevin: that matches an eviction+warmup race where many cold requests all miss and hit backend simultaneously (thundering herd). did we have prefetch warmup disabled? 
anya: warmup was on but we reduced warmup parallelism in the config pushed in the rollout to avoid saturating small GPUs. looks like we under-provisioned warmup which made misses cascade. 
yuki: confirmed redis 6.2 late-acks and increased active connections around same time. also saw kernel selection fallback to generic kernels after warmup failed, which raised token CPU per step. 
mike: profiling snippet: 
```
hot path: kv_get -> misses -> backend_decode -> kernel_generic_attention (higher flops)
cold path token cost ~2.5x warm path
```
kevin: so two factors: eviction policy too aggressive + warmup concurrency cut -> stampede. suggests we should add jittered backoff and single-flight de-dup of warmups (one warmup per prefix per node). 
anya: agreed. we also saw a bad cache keying pattern: some clients send prompt trimming that produces semantically identical prefixes with trailing whitespace differences -> cache fragmentation. example keys differ by suffix "\\n" or not. 
sre-oncall: initiated emergency step: disabled distributed prefix caching for the affected pool (pool-13) at 07:18 UTC. traffic fell back to local LRU and backend load stabilized. open to revert once fix is validated. :warning: 
ops-bot: deploybot: rollback runtime-2.3.1 -> runtime-2.3.0 initiated by @sre-oncall at 07:21 UTC. status: in progress. 
yuki: quick mitigation suggestions: 
- enable single-flight warmup (mutex per prefix)
- add random jitter on warmup start (10-100ms)
- extend TTL for hot prefixes temporarily + bump max_cached_entries
- normalize prompt keying (trim whitespace, collapse repeated tokens)
- make warmup concurrency adaptive to node free memory instead of fixed cap
kevin: long term: add a cache hit-rate circuit breaker that temporarily falls back to local-only when hit-rate drops > X% in Y seconds, and an observable for warmup queue length. also add model/kernel selection metric (generic vs optimized) to perf dashboards. 
mike: I'll draft a PR for single-flight warmup + key-normalizer. also add a migration that sets hot-prefix TTL from 5m->20m for service-critical routes. 
anya: record action items: 
1) mike: PR for single-flight warmup + key normalization (ETA 4h)
2) kevin: dashboard panels for warmup queue / kernel-fallbacks / hit-rate alerts (ETA 2h)
3) yuki: run redis healthcheck + tune conn limits (ETA 1h)
4) sre-oncall: keep cache disabled on pool-13 until rollout validated (standing)
5) ops-bot/deploy-bot: coordinate staged re-enable once canary hit-rate stable

thanks all, this felt like an eviction+warmup race amplified by keying noise and kernel fallbacks. followups in #eng-runtime infra-epic. :thumbsup:
